item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00130","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C05","C11"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.91,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C12 plausibly supplied material drafting components for the child’s treatment of military household-goods shipments. It contains the same specialized definition encompassing baggage, household effects, and professional books, papers, and equipment; establishes Government-paid transportation subject to authorized weight allowances; and makes the owner responsible for excess quantities. The child adapts that machinery to payment of general-average contributions and extends it to civilian employees. C05 and C11 are also relevant, especially to the child’s commuted-basis exclusion for civilian shipments, but they provide a narrower portion of the resulting order.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The term \"household goods\" means such baggage, household goods, and effects, including privately-owned automobiles and professional books, papers, and equipment, of military personnel and civilian employees as are authorized to be transported at Government expense by law or regulation pursuant to law.","parent_excerpt":"Household goods, clothing, baggage, and all other personal effects of a similar character (including professional books, papers and equipment see par. 3) ...","explanation":"The shared specialized enumeration, particularly “professional books, papers, and equipment,” indicates reuse of the earlier military household-goods regulatory vocabulary."},{"child_excerpt":"Whenever military personnel or civilian employees ... are liable for general-average contributions arising out of shipments of household goods ... authorized or approved under law or regulations pursuant to law, disbursements shall be made ... from appropriations chargeable for the transportation of baggage and household goods and effects.","parent_excerpt":"Household goods ... not in excess of the weight limits ... may be shipped at government expense in accordance with the provisions of these regulations.","explanation":"Both use the same administrative framework: Government-funded benefits tied to legally authorized household-goods transportation and bounded by prescribed shipment allowances."},{"child_excerpt":"To quantities of household goods ... shipped in excess of quantities authorized to be transported by law or regulation pursuant to law. In any case of such excess shipment, the liability of the Government ... shall not exceed the proportion that the applicable limitation, by weight or volume, bears to the total quantity ... shipped.","parent_excerpt":"Where shipments involve weights in excess of the prescribed allowance ... the transportation charges on such excess weights ... will be borne by the owner.","explanation":"The child adapts C12’s substantive excess-shipment limitation to allocate general-average liability proportionally rather than transportation charges directly."}]}
